body:
Roster group R10-FLOW-PULL (Lean flow study K3 and K10): pull, pitch and classes of service in the orchestrator's turn. Prose-only change to `dev/governance/roles/nudge.md` and `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md`; no cap file changes, every added sentence paid by a cut in the same file.

`nudge.md`:
- Step 16 dispatches by pull: a flow lane under its cap (A critical path 4, B product 4, C process 3, F fly-in 2) takes its eligible group of greatest critical-path depth, behind `tools/audit/seat/pr_cap.py` dispatch-gate, which enforces the total. A fly-in is registered at dispatch with `tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py` append-group under a name starting `R10-FLY-` (no new kind, no schema change). An expedite item (red main, quota exhaustion, outage, security) bypasses the caps, one at a time.
- Steps 3 and 7: the train loads on the hourly pitch with `--bot-prs`; one verdicted pull request is still a train, and the record pull request merges inside the pitch. Step 7 keeps only the direct merge of a budgets-file or policy-path pull request whose mandate review is on that head.
- Steps 1 and 2: the reviewer still starts at handoff, without waiting for required checks; the verdict posts once required checks have concluded at that head; a head that moved since a merge verdict goes to `tools/pr/app_approve.sh --carry` first and gets a reviewer only when the carry refuses.
- Step 6 shrinks to its exception: the nightly record beat merges a `record:` pull request when its approver token is present (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, the automerge step's `say` outcomes), so a hand merge is owed only on a `skip-` outcome other than `skip-train-hold`.
- Step 9: absorb `origin/main` into an open head only when it is DIRTY or `git merge-tree --write-tree` reports a conflict; a head merely behind `main` stays put.
- Step 12 is unchanged: the brief shrinks it only once R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE lands, and that group's resume stage is not-started (carried below).

`orchestrator.md`:
- Section 5 keeps the sentence dispatching a fix's reviewer when the fixer pushes, and gains the chain rule (a serial chain orders groups whose owning seams overlap, not groups that share a file) and the scope freeze (a mid-round finding goes to the next round's register unless it is expedite or a size-S fly-in).
- Section 6's DIRTY sentence now names step 9's absorb trigger; section 11's duplicate of it ("a `DIRTY` pull request never queues Tests") is cut, since section 6 states it.

Payments, all deletions of prose stated elsewhere or of motivation: nudge step 3's "There is no `tools/audit/merge_train.py`" pair (the next sentence and step 3's first line name the real path), step 8's restatement of the four-prepr train condition step 3 already carries, step 17's "not the handover" (step 12 says it), step 16's "A deferred group stays deferred" (the eligibility list excludes deferred); orchestrator section 10b's restatement of `brief-citations.md`'s tag-citation remedy, and two motivational clauses in section 5.

## Head

`8a009877502b384ea0460855c44993c826f6080a` merges main `cf01e82` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`ced4bf66e91d3c61254066c310f1f9af7ea064ef` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/2628.md`. The authored code head is `de20d0c7206b2f73ccf4702229dba50d47fb8d1c`.

de20d0c7206b2f73ccf4702229dba50d47fb8d1c, on merge base de69745ffcab66b566b3e75aee0b572023f80857 (`origin/main`'s tip at 2026-10-22T21:34Z).

## Approval

This changes policy (`nudge.md`, `orchestrator.md`). The roster's owner gate: tvofi's approving review before merge (`CLAUDE.md`); the mandate on #201, comment 6175172275, covers it until 2026-10-28T18:14Z, after which a fresh grant is needed. The roster carries name the owner rulings this text encodes and owes: takt and pitch, lane caps, records in the pitch, the absorb trigger, the fly-in and expedite rule (Lean flow pre-study, section R). No cap is raised.

## Mutation proof

The text has no detector of its own; the check it moves is `policy_lint.mjs`'s budgets arm, with `nudge.md` at its line cap and 2 tokens under its token cap after this diff. Mutant: one sentence appended to `nudge.md`, then `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` exits 1 with two `[budgets]` errors for nudge.md (116 lines over 115; about 3820 tokens over 3814). Restored: exit 0.

## Null control

`node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` at the merge base, in a detached worktree of `origin/main`: `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 43 policy file(s)`, the same line the head prints, so the head adds no error the base lacks.

## Figures

- `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets`: the nudge.md and orchestrator.md rows and the corpus line, read at base and head; neither file exceeds its cap at the head, and the corpus stays under its cap without the band.
- `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`: exit 0 at the head and at the base.
- `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs --check`: exit 0 (no rule file changed).
- `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs`: exit 0.
- `python3 -I tools/policy/agreement_py.py --out <json>` then `node tools/policy/agreement.mjs --py-json <json>`: `AGREEMENT ok`, with the branch copy and with `origin/main`'s copy of `tools/policy/agreement.mjs` (the copy CI grades with); `--self-test` exit 0.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff <merge base>`: `MODE: SCOPED`, `scope.run` names `tests/entities.py`; it and `tests/run.sh`'s `run_always` scripts (`env_drift.py --claims-only`, `closure.py selftest`, `layout.py`, `harness_headers.py`) and `tests/structure.py` ran under the seat venv's Python, results in the entities line below.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python tests/entities.py` exit 0, last line `ALL ... ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (the count is the instrument's); `tests/harness_headers.py`, `tests/layout.py`, `tests/closure.py selftest`, `tests/structure.py` and `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only <merge base>` each exit 0.

## Red checks

none

## Forward-carry

- Step 12 of `nudge.md` is to shrink to its exceptions when the after-merge bookkeeping lands; this pull request leaves it whole because that group is not done. Landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `1f35f6d2054fdf054cb91c45f8c5da997a8956f9`. Carry: R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE
- `tools/audit/seat/sweep_template.md` item (3), a generator of the orchestrator's sweep prompt, still describes loading verdicted pull requests into one batch with no hourly pitch and no `--bot-prs`; the group that mechanises the pitch owns that template's merge line. The roster edit is the orchestrator's (this seat writes only its return refs). Landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `d0b49bc68cd571d006a5b62f3907f6a550244b4f`. Carry: R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN
- From review 6fc4c91ab: `nudge.md` step 16 still holds a ready critical-path group behind its lane cap and the WIP total, against tvofi's 2026-10-22 rulings. Landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `5a762df2ea9c848da2fb7d806d1e38edbb8beefc`, the roster tip carrying all three (`brief_lint.mjs` exits 0 there; they reach main with roster batch 17). Carry: R10-FLOW-ARCH-PLANNER

## Friction

none

Fix review: blocked ced4bf66e91d3c61254066c310f1f9af7ea064ef carry-missing: not carried to R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE or R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN

bus-nonce: 88919d7150283ca7b820a8d4186cd07d

Round 1. Reviewed from a detached worktree at ced4bf66e91d3c61254066c310f1f9af7ea064ef, against merge base de69745ffcab66b566b3e75aee0b572023f80857 (= origin/main when reviewed). The head was re-read from the PR before writing this verdict, and it had not moved. Roles were current: `git diff <merge-base>...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` was empty.

## Block

- fix-review.md step 10 and finding-propagation.md "Enforcement" say a producing PR does not merge until its carry is in the tree, and that the body names the roster branch SHA. The body's `## Forward-carry` names two destinations. Neither is on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at ddd2e8de9c50e5a56164ba8a29459c6b4e41a65b, and the body names no roster SHA.
  - R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE. Its brief describes the four after-merge steps. It does not say that nudge.md step 12 then shrinks to its exceptions, which is the residue of this group's own brief.
  - R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN. Its brief and carries do not mention `tools/audit/seat/sweep_template.md` item (3). After this PR, that item still describes one batch of verdicted PRs with no hourly pitch and no `--bot-prs`, which disagrees with nudge.md step 3.
- The body says the seat cannot write the roster (decision 0011/0013 identity). The remedy is therefore the orchestrator's:
  1. Land both carries with `roster_edit.py` on the roster branch and read them back with `brief_lint.mjs`.
  2. Add that roster SHA to the body.
  3. Re-review. The head does not need to move.
- Nothing else in this review blocks.

## Findings

- nudge.md step 16, as written at this head, holds a ready critical-path group behind two caps:
  - its flow-lane cap ("A critical path 4");
  - `pr_cap.py dispatch-gate`, which refuses at HPO_WIP_CAP (default 6) unless given `--over-cap <reason>`.

  Only expedite items (red main, quota exhaustion, outage, security) bypass the caps. That contradicts the owner rulings of 2026-10-22: "ready critical-path groups are exempt from the open-PR soft cap" and "remember critical path groups starts regardless off the caps when ready".

  R10-FLOW-ARCH-PLANNER already carries the first ruling, but only for orchestrator.md section 5's soft-cap bullet. Precondition for that group: nudge.md step 16 must also state that a ready critical-path group (a member of the plan's `critical_path`, every `after` group done) is dispatched regardless of its lane cap and the WIP total, via `pr_cap.py dispatch-gate --over-cap "critical path: <group>"`. The same `--over-cap` route should be named for expedite items. Control: no sentence in nudge.md or orchestrator.md conditions a ready critical-path dispatch on any cap. Carry: R10-FLOW-ARCH-PLANNER
- The lane caps (A4, B4, C3, F2) and the `R10-FLY-` fly-in naming are prose only. `pr_cap.py` has no notion of lane or fly-in and enforces only the roster-group WIP total (6). Because the lane caps sum to 13, above that total, they bind only within a lane. This matches the PR's own wording ("which enforces the total"), so it is not a defect here. Mechanising lane accounting is a design choice for the group that mechanises dispatch. Carry: dismissed: the wording states accurately what pr_cap.py enforces; lane caps as prose are the owner-adopted Lean study's choice, not a contradiction

## Evidence

- Head and merge:
  - Head checked at start and before writing: ced4bf66e91d3c61254066c310f1f9af7ea064ef (`ev/HEAD.txt`).
  - It is the authored head de20d0c7 plus one delivery-row commit (`dev/programme/delivery/2628.md`), as the body says.
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` exited 0 with tree 9f71d275513a115e36f34fd0f450c7b4e0e6473c, so there are no conflicts (`ev/merge_tree.txt`).
- Budgets, with `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --budgets` (`ev/budgets_head.txt`, `ev/budgets_base.txt`):
  - nudge.md is 115/115 lines and ~3812/3814 tokens at both base and head (15249 bytes at base, 15246 at head). It is flat at its cap.
  - orchestrator.md goes from 316 lines, ~4481 tokens at base to 317, ~4512 at head (caps 319 and 4513).
  - The corpus goes from ~62857 to ~62888 tokens (cap 62892, under it without the band).
  - The body's figures match these.
- Mutation proof, re-run: I appended one sentence to nudge.md. `policy_lint.mjs` then exited 1 with two `[budgets]` errors: 116 lines against the 115 cap, and about 3822 tokens against 3814. After restoring, it exits 0 (`ev/mutant_append.txt`). The body's "about 3820" is approximate and consistent. The text has no content detector: a mutant to a sentence's meaning (for example dropping `--bot-prs`) is caught by nothing, and the body says so.
- Null control, re-run: `policy_lint.mjs` prints `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 43 policy file(s)` at both base and head (`ev/lint_head.txt`, `ev/lint_base.txt`). `rules_sync.mjs --check` exits 0. `brief_lint.mjs` exits 0. I did not re-run the agreement and entities lines.
- Wording against the tools:
  - `pr_cap.py dispatch-gate` exists and enforces a total WIP cap.
  - `roster_edit.py append-group` exists.
  - `merge_train.py --bot-prs` exists, and merges record/autofix PRs inside the train.
  - `app_approve.sh --carry` exists.
  - The nightly record beat's `say skip-train-hold` exists (nightly.yml line 978), as do `skip-no-approver` and the other `skip-` outcomes the body cites.
- Cuts the body says are restated elsewhere, each checked:
  - Step 8's four-prepr train condition is in step 3.
  - Step 17's "not the handover" is in step 12.
  - Section 6 keeps "a `DIRTY` pull request never queues Tests".
  - The eligibility list excludes deferred groups.
- Version: neither `VERSION`, the manifest nor `RELEASE_NOTES.md` is touched. No claim file or golden fixture is touched, so step 4 is not applicable.
- CI on this head, from the check-runs API (`ev/check_runs.tsv`):
  - Every concluded check is success or skipped, except `nightly-status`, and `coverage` and `fast (3.14)` were still in progress when this was written.
  - `nightly-status` is red. It reads the last scheduled run of nightly.yml and grades main. This diff (two role files and a delivery row) does not reach what it reads, so it is not this PR's red. It is not a required check and does not block.
- Owner gate: policy paths need tvofi's approving review, or the mandate 6175172275 (until 2026-10-28T18:14Z). It is outside this verdict.

- RESULT diff: three-dot diff touches only dev/governance/roles/nudge.md, dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md and dev/programme/delivery/2628.md; VERSION, manifest version and RELEASE_NOTES untouched.

The only failure is nightly-status, which grades main; the diff touches none of what it reads, so it is not this PR's and the body owes it no answer (defect-root-cause.md). - Not re-run (round 1 stands, head unmoved): mutation proof, null control, figures in the body; I did not re-derive them this round.
